newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes subdued, May talk at snail's pace.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes subdued, May talk at snail's pace.

text.p: North Sea crude differentials were broadly unchanged on Wednesday as early May talk got off to a slow start, traders said.

Of the eight main North Sea systems, only the Flotta loading programme was still to be released but traders saw little sign of the usual rush of interest for early month cargoes left after equity producers and term customers have taken their pick.
"It's been extremely quiet today, there's been very little interest in the first decade," said a trader.
Trade was restricted to an end-month April Oseberg and two early May stems of minor North Sea grades Beryl and DUC.

Dated Brent sentiment was subdued with two of the first three May cargoes clocked, but some dealers said one of the cargoes was being offered at around June Brent -62 cents, equivalent to a firmer May Brent -35 cents.

June Brent paper shed 18 cents to $17.96 a barrel by 1730 GMT, depressed by evidence of rising U.S. inventories and intermonth spreads were also a shade softer, June/July slipping a cent to trade at -16 cents.
U.S. crude inventories rose by between 2.5 and 3.0 million barrels last week, according to data released by the American Petroleum Institute and the U.S. Department of Energy.
In the Mediterranean, Russian Urals was talked steady at Dated Brent -$1.15/-$1.10 but traders said they suspected it may ease further if three unsold April cargoes remain on offer.
"Urals is being talked -$1.15, -$1.10...If there's a few more cargoes to be sold then I suspect it will come under more pressure," a trader said.
Negotiations for Syrian May term prices continued with state oil company Sytrol asking Dated Brent -82 cents for Syrian Light with buyers bidding 8-13 cents a barrel cheaper.
"I think the people will hope for a rollover, but whether the Syrians will give, I don't know...If Urals comes under further pressure then I suspect the buyers will hold back," the trader said.
The West African market remained quiet after the release of Nigerian May term prices.
Traders said state Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) set Bonny Light and Qua Iboe (BQ) for May at Dated Brent plus 15 cents, up from Dated Brent plus four cents in April.
Forcados for May was set at Dated Brent -30 cents compared to Brent -40 cents in April while Brass River went up 16 cents to Brent plus 25 cents.
"There were no deals in the (West African) market," one trader said, adding that about 10 million barrels of West African grades were still on offer in April.
